name: Bicrypto

scripts.build:frontend: cross-env NODE_ENV=production NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 pnpm build:i18n && pnpm --filter frontend build
scripts.//gate: There is no CI in this repo. `pnpm gate` IS the CI: it runs the drift gates (routes, addon menus, permissions.json, stale files), eslint over the DEX trees, the unit lanes, and the red-run evidence check. `gate:fast` is what the tracked pre-push hook runs; `gate:full` adds the backend typecheck. Run `pnpm hooks:install` once per clone to arm the hook - there is deliberately no `prepare` script, because pnpm would run it during a customer's `pnpm updator` on a zip with no .git.
scripts.//check-permission: TWO halves of one contract, so ONE script checks both. build-permission.js --check compares the FRONTEND route manifest against the permission.ts sources; check-route-permissions.js compares every BACKEND route's `permission:` metadata against the seeder's permissionsList. The second exists because the seeder is the only writer to the `permission` table, so a key it does not list is UNGRANTABLE and rolesGate 403s every non-Super-Admin forever, silently.
scripts.check:permission: node tools/build-permission.js --check && node tools/check-route-permissions.js --self-test && node tools/check-route-permissions.js
scripts.//api-inventory: The frozen NON-ADMIN endpoint list the native mobile app is built against (mobile/plan/03-BACKEND-GAPS.md §3.1), so no phase of that programme cites a path from memory. Derived from the same filename rules backend/src/handler/Routes.ts uses — parsed from source, never by booting, because the loader skips a route whose import throws and those are exactly the addon routes worth recording. Canonical copy is tracked here; mobile/references/ gets a mirror when present, since this repo .gitignores mobile/.
scripts.//initial-sql: initial.sql is the schema a FRESH install imports, and the seeders run against it BEFORE anything syncs — so a table it is missing is not a slow boot, it is a failed install. It is therefore GENERATED from backend/models, never hand-edited. `check:initial-sql` compares table names from source and runs inside `pnpm gate`; `initial-sql:check` also catches column/index/enum drift but needs a reachable MySQL, which is why it is separate.
scripts.//mutate: Mutation sweep: breaks a file on purpose and reports which breaks the suite does not notice. NOT a gate step — it rewrites source files while it runs, which is unsafe in a shared worktree and in CI without isolation. Run it deliberately, read the survivors, turn each into an assertion. It proves a green baseline first and aborts if the runner never reached the tests, because an all-red sweep is what a BROKEN runner produces.
scripts.//check:source-bytes: A raw NUL byte makes ripgrep classify a source file as BINARY and skip it, so every repo-wide scan in this tree silently misses it. Nine tracked files carried one. The fix is always to rewrite the byte as its escape - identical at runtime - never a suppression.
scripts.//check:superseded: A function replaced because the old one was money-wrong keeps its callers unless something enforces the move. An emergency stop and a copy-trading cancel each read ONE Scylla page and reported an account clear while orders sat funded and resting.
scripts.//build:chart-engine: `npm --prefix` rather than `cd`, for two reasons. The path contains PARENTHESES, and a bare `cd frontend/components/(ext)/chart-engine` is a syntax error under any PowerShell script-shell - it only ever worked because npm defaults to cmd.exe on Windows, so setting script-shell to pwsh broke the addon build with a parse error that names neither npm nor the addon. And `--prefix` needs no `cd` at all, so the working directory is never left changed for whatever runs next in a chained script. `--no-audit --no-fund` keep a build step from making two network round-trips it has no use for; `.npmrc` in the addon already stops npm installing the peers.
scripts.start: node scripts/maintenance-off.js && node scripts/reconcile-scheduler.js production.config.js && cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 pm2 start production.config.js --env production
scripts.start:thread: node scripts/maintenance-off.js && node scripts/reconcile-scheduler.js production.thread.config.js && cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 pm2 start production.thread.config.js --env production
scripts.start:backend: node scripts/maintenance-off.js && node scripts/reconcile-scheduler.js production.backend.config.js && cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 pm2 start production.backend.config.js --env production
scripts.updator: pnpm stop && node scripts/ensure-deps.mjs && pnpm updator:migrate && pnpm seed && pnpm build:frontend && pnpm start
scripts.//updator-install-not-update: `pnpm install`, NOT `pnpm update-packages-quick`. Applying a release means making node_modules match the package.json + lockfile that release shipped. `pnpm update` instead bumps every dependency to the newest version its range allows, which fights the pins in pnpm-workspace.yaml (it resolved @wagmi/core 2.22.1 against a 2.21.2 override on a real install) and churns the virtual store for no reason. update-packages-quick is still available to run deliberately.
scripts.//updator-migrate: The Node migration backend is the ONLY backend `pnpm updator` may use. There is deliberately no RUST_MIGRATE branch here: `bicrypto-ops migrate` is not wired into the customer update chain until v7, when the Rust backend is complete and Node has stopped alter-syncing at boot. Until then Sequelize still shapes the schema at start, so a Rust apply would be a second writer against the same tables on a live install. scripts/updator-migrate.js already prints the UPDATE HALTED wording (scripts/updator-migrate.js:168-203) and exits non-zero, which is what stops the chain before `pnpm seed` and `pnpm start` run against a half-migrated schema.
scripts.update-packages-quick: pnpm --filter backend update && pnpm --filter frontend update && pnpm update
scripts.i18n: cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 cd tools/translation-manager && npm start
scripts.fix:eco-orders: cd backend && cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 node scripts/fix-ecosystem-orders.mjs
scripts.//eco:candle:doctor: READ-ONLY forensics for ONE market's candle series: rows filed off their UTC interval boundary by the old local-time normaliser, duplicate buckets, price outliers cross-checked against ecosystem.trades, and how far the newest candle trails the tape. `eco:candle:doctor:fix` deletes ONLY rows that are both off-boundary and shadowed by an on-boundary row for the same bucket - never an outlier, never a lone row. Pass the market through npm: `npm run eco:candle:doctor -- --symbol BTC/USDT`.
scripts.reconcile:eco-inorder: cd backend && cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 node scripts/reconcile-eco-inorder.mjs
scripts.fix:eco-candles: cd backend && cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 node scripts/fix-ecosystem-candles.mjs
scripts.rebuild:eco-orderbook: cd backend && cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 node scripts/rebuild-eco-orderbook.mjs
scripts.db:migrate:6.4.9:before: cd backend && node scripts/migration-ecosys06-broadcast-hash-lock.mjs && node scripts/deduplicate-kyc-applications.mjs && node scripts/dedupe-nft-sale-hashes.mjs
scripts.db:migrate:6.4.9:before:apply: cd backend && node scripts/migration-ecosys06-broadcast-hash-lock.mjs --apply && node scripts/deduplicate-kyc-applications.mjs --apply && node scripts/dedupe-nft-sale-hashes.mjs --apply
scripts.db:migrate:6.4.9:after: cd backend && node scripts/drop-investment-unique-index.mjs && node scripts/fix-gateway-merchant-indexes.mjs && node scripts/fix-fk-on-delete.mjs && node scripts/retire-staking-pool-legacy.mjs && node scripts/backfill-method-status.mjs && node scripts/add-wallet-address-lookup.mjs && node scripts/add-transfer-spread-setting.mjs
scripts.db:migrate:6.4.9:after:apply: cd backend && node scripts/drop-investment-unique-index.mjs --apply && node scripts/fix-gateway-merchant-indexes.mjs --apply && node scripts/fix-fk-on-delete.mjs --apply && node scripts/retire-staking-pool-legacy.mjs --apply && node scripts/backfill-method-status.mjs --apply && node scripts/add-wallet-address-lookup.mjs --apply && node scripts/add-transfer-spread-setting.mjs --apply
scripts.//db-migrate-6.6.3: The 6.6.3 data repairs, dry-run by default. migration-json-column-unwrap is the BROAD one — 18 tables, including wallet.address, user.profile, both method customFields, support_ticket and thirteen NFT tables — and it was missing from this script, so an operator who followed the release note repaired ecosystem_token and the recovery codes and nothing else. It runs FIRST because it is the one whose absence is felt outside the model layer: the getters unwrap a stray layer, so a double-encoded row still reads correctly THROUGH the model, but a `raw: true` query sees the text. migration-user-profile-json-unwrap is deliberately NOT listed — user.profile is already in the broad script's target table and running both would be one pass wasted, not two repairs. It stays on disk as a standalone for anyone repairing that column alone. All four are idempotent: a value that already parses to an object or array is left untouched, so re-running costs a read.
scripts.db:migrate:6.6.3: cd backend && node scripts/migration-json-column-unwrap.mjs && node scripts/migration-eco-token-json-unwrap.mjs && node scripts/migration-hash-recovery-codes.mjs
scripts.db:migrate:6.6.3:apply: cd backend && node scripts/migration-json-column-unwrap.mjs --apply && node scripts/migration-eco-token-json-unwrap.mjs --apply && node scripts/migration-hash-recovery-codes.mjs --apply
scripts.//db-migrate-6.6.4: The two 6.6.4 settings migrations, in the order the release note runs them, dry-run by default. `pnpm updator` cannot apply either: each reads a value only the operator's database knows — the legacy withdrawApproval row, and whether the install already has users — and pins the behaviour that install ALREADY HAS rather than a default. Both are idempotent, so a second run costs a read. reconcile-eco-chain-trackers.ts is deliberately NOT here: it repairs custody-tracker rows written by a bug, not an upgrade step, so it must not run on every install that upgrades — it stays the direct tsx invocation the release note documents, aliased in backend/package.json as `repair:eco-chain-trackers`.
scripts.db:migrate:6.6.4: cd backend && node scripts/migrate-withdraw-auto-approve.mjs && node scripts/backfill-verify-email-status.mjs
scripts.db:migrate:6.6.4:apply: cd backend && node scripts/migrate-withdraw-auto-approve.mjs --apply && node scripts/backfill-verify-email-status.mjs --apply
scripts.//db-migrate-6.7.3: The KYC document migration, dry-run by default. It is here for the same reason every other release s data step is: prose in a release note was the only thing carrying it, and 6.7.2 shipped that prose INVERTED. 6.7.2 closed /uploads/kyc permanently at BOTH doors — backend serveStaticFile and the frontend beforeFiles rewrite — so every document already on disk stops resolving the moment the release is deployed, for the applicant AND for the operator s own KYC reviewers, and the card just fails to load. This is the step that ends that window. Paths resolve from __dirname, so `cd backend` changes nothing. Safe to re-run: it copies and verifies by size before it unlinks, and sweeps unreferenced files to _orphaned/ rather than deleting evidence an operator may be required to retain. Set KYC_DOCUMENT_DIR in .env BEFORE applying if the store belongs on another volume.
scripts.//bundle-permissions: extract:permission rebuilds the permission REGISTRY (which keys exist) from the frontend permission.ts files; build:permission rebuilds the route MANIFEST (which route requires which key) from the same files. Only the first used to run here, so the keys regenerated every release and the gates never did — they drifted to 185 committed entries against 217 generated. Both now run, in that order, so source is the single truth. NOTE gates ship STRICT: middlewares/auth.ts:246 fails closed, so a newly gated screen is reachable by Super Admin only (it bypasses by name) until an operator grants the key per role in Admin -> Roles — the same step a new addon needs. `pnpm check:permission` reports drift without writing, and lists which screens are waiting on a grant so they can go in the release notes.
scripts.bundle: pnpm extract:permission && pnpm build:permission && pnpm build:chart-engine && node -e "require('fs').rmSync('backend/dist',{recursive:true,force:true})" && pnpm build:backend && pnpm ob
scripts.//gate:icons: Icons must be on disk. The old <Icon> fetched its set from api.iconify.design when it mounted, so a firewalled operator got blank pages and every visitor's browser called a third party. Three files had already worked that out and fixed only themselves; 141 had not. This fails the build on any remaining CDN import AND on any icon name the local registry cannot resolve — because a local glyph, unlike a fetched one, cannot be conjured at runtime.
scripts.//gate:dupes: Parses every .ts in the tree and refuses a scope that declares the same name twice - i.e. an edit applied on top of itself. It exists because `tsc` is the only other thing that catches it (TS2451) and the backend typecheck is `gate:full` only, so the break can otherwise be committed and pushed. Also runs on staged files from the pre-commit hook.
scripts.dev:concurrent: cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7780 concurrently "pnpm --filter frontend dev" "pnpm --filter backend dev"
scripts.//sbom: CRA Annex I Part II(1): top-level dependency SBOM in CycloneDX. --check is a gate step.
scripts.//check:template-claims: The page-builder templates ship inside the product: an operator drags a section onto their live site and publishes our copy verbatim, about a financial product, in their name. The tree shipped FIX 4.4 support, Singapore colocation, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PwC audits and fourteen 99.99% uptime SLAs. None of it exists. A manual grep missed eight of them, which is why this is a script and not a habit.

//pnpm: Dependency settings (overrides, peerDependencyRules, onlyBuiltDependencies, ignoredBuiltDependencies) live in pnpm-workspace.yaml. pnpm 10 no longer reads a "pnpm" field here — it warns and IGNORES it, so re-adding one silently drops every override.
